targets.title: Branding alters attitude functions and reduces the advantage of function-matching persuasive appeals.
targets.evidence_quote: Push button reproduction attempt of a research claim from LeBoeuf et al. (2010)
targets.outcome_computational_quote: Reproduction result: Confirmed. Products predominantly associated with utilitarian attitudes at the category-level supported more symbolic attitudes when branded, whereas products predominantly associated with symbolic attitudes at the category-level supported less symbolic attitudes when branded. A 2 (level: category or brand) × 2 (unbranded product type: utilitarian or symbolic) mixed ANOVA on the difference scores (averaged for each product type) revealed the predicted level × product type interaction (F(1, 204) = 7.70, p = .006).
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: Description of materials provided: An .R script for the analyses was provided as well as a .csv file containing the data. To reproduce the focal test, the analyst needs both the Study 1b Data .csv file and the .R script.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The push-button analysis recovers the exact focal F and p values. The report only reruns the supplied analysis; it reports no alternative specifications.
